Paper: [Gu and Dao, arXiv:2312.00752v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752v2).
The exported Mamba notes and State-Space Models slides motivate the mathematical background in [state-space models](../../study-notes/machine-learning/state-space-models.qmd).

## Problem

A fixed convolution kernel can retain information according to its age, but its coefficients do not change according to the content of each new token.
This makes selective retention and content-dependent recall difficult for an LTI sequence layer.
Attention supports content-dependent routing, but standard full attention has quadratic work in sequence length and a growing history cache during generation.

## Previous Attempts

[S4](../../study-notes/machine-learning/state-space-models.qmd#s4) uses structured dynamics to evaluate a sequence layer as a convolution during training and as a recurrence during generation.
The convolution route relies on fixed parameters across positions.
Mamba keeps a recurrent state while changing which state-space parameters depend on the current input.

## Proposed Solution

Write $u_t$ for the input activation at one position and $h_t$ for a per-channel state.
Algorithm 2 makes $B_t$, $C_t$, and the positive step size $\Delta_t$ functions of the input.
The continuous base matrix $A$ remains a learned parameter shared across positions.

$$
  \begin{aligned}
  B_t&=s_B(u_t),\\
  C_t&=s_C(u_t),\\
  \Delta_t&=\operatorname{softplus}(b+s_\Delta(u_t)).
  \end{aligned}
$$

Discretisation then makes $\bar A_t$ and $\bar B_t$ input-dependent.
The state update and readout have the form

$$
  \begin{aligned}
  h_t&=\bar A_t h_{t-1}+\bar B_tu_t,\\
  y_t&=C_th_t.
  \end{aligned}
$$

For the ZOH construction in Equation 4, $\bar A_t=\exp(\Delta_tA)$.
The [discretisation note](../../study-notes/machine-learning/state-space-models.qmd#discretisation) gives the matching input coefficient.
The full Mamba block adds projections, a local convolution, nonlinearities, a gated branch, and an output projection around the selective SSM.
These surrounding operations make the network more than an isolated linear recurrence; see Figure 3.

The generic expression “keep a fraction of the old state and inject a fraction of the input” is useful intuition, but a sigmoid gate multiplying two fixed matrices is not a complete statement of Mamba's parameterisation.
In particular, $C_t$ also depends on the input, and $\Delta_t$ changes the discretised transition even though $A$ is shared.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false" title="Derivation: why affine recurrence supports a parallel scan"}

For a fixed input sequence, each position defines an affine map $F_t(h)=M_th+b_t$.
Composing two successive maps gives

$$
  (M_2,b_2)\circ(M_1,b_1)
  =(M_2M_1,\;M_2b_1+b_2).
$$

For three maps, either grouping yields transition $M_3M_2M_1$ and offset

$$
  M_3M_2b_1+M_3b_2+b_3.
$$

Composition is therefore associative, so prefix compositions can be computed with a parallel scan.
The operation is generally not commutative: token order still matters.
For a diagonal transition, matrix products reduce to elementwise products, supporting efficient per-channel state updates.
Input dependence removes the fixed convolution kernel but does not remove this associativity.

:::

The hardware implementation combines scan, kernel fusion, and recomputation to avoid repeatedly materialising the full expanded state in GPU high-bandwidth memory.
Thus the algorithmic claim concerns both the recurrence and memory traffic; merely writing a parallel scan in a high-level loop does not establish the same runtime.
These details are in Section 3.3 and Appendix D.

## Evidence

Selective copying and induction-head tasks test whether the model retains or retrieves information based on content rather than a fixed offset.
The paper also evaluates language, audio, and genomics modelling, with efficiency measurements in Section 4.5.
Its reported throughput advantages belong to the specified models, sequence lengths, hardware, and batching conditions.
They are not a universal speed ratio against every Transformer implementation.

## Limitations

At fixed width and state dimension, sequence work grows linearly with length and recurrent state size is independent of the number of processed tokens.
That fixed state still compresses history; it is not exact storage of every prior token.
The full network is nonlinear in its input, even though the state update is affine when the input-dependent coefficients are held fixed.
Stable scalar decay coefficients alone do not prove bounded behaviour of every trained block under arbitrary input or unbounded readout gains.

## Connections

[Matrix structure](../../study-notes/mathematics/matrix-dynamics.qmd#properties) separates asymptotic stability, transient amplification, and diagonalisation.
[Attention and KV caching](../../study-notes/machine-learning/kv-cache.qmd#kv-cache) explain the different way an attention model retains history.
[HiPPO](../../study-notes/machine-learning/state-space-models.qmd#hippo) derives memory coefficients from a projection problem; Mamba does not guarantee that every learned state retains that exact polynomial interpretation.
